title: Electronic conductivity of solid electrolytes causes physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries - Nature Energy
gist: Wang, Xu, Zhong et al. show that the residual electronic conductivity of inorganic solid-state electrolytes, typically 10^-8 to 10^-9 S cm^-1, drives considerable physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries — most severely at the tens-of-micrometres electrolyte thickness needed for competitive energy density — and that suppressing it requires roughly 10^-12 S cm^-1, a threshold no prevalent solid electrolyte currently meets. Only the abstract, figure captions and author/funding metadata are accessible in this record; the quantitative body is behind a paywall preview.

insights.claim: The residual electronic conductivity of inorganic solid-state electrolytes, typically in the range of 10^-8 to 10^-9 S cm^-1, causes considerable physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries — a loss channel distinct from the chemical shuttle mechanisms studied in liquid-electrolyte cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Introduces a first-principles ceiling on ASSB shelf life and calendar performance that materials selection alone, as currently practised, does not clear.
insights.quote: we reveal that the electronic conductivity of SSEs, typically in the range of 10−8–10−9 S cm−1, contributes to considerable physical self-discharge in ASSBs

insights.claim: Physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries becomes pronounced specifically when the solid electrolyte separator thickness is on the order of tens of micrometres — precisely the thin-separator regime required for the high energy density that motivates the technology.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Creates a direct engineering trade-off between ASSB energy density and shelf life; thick-separator lab cells will systematically overstate real-world self-discharge performance.
insights.quote: particularly when the SSE thickness is on the order of tens of micrometres

insights.claim: The self-discharge behaviour of all-solid-state batteries — described by the authors as a critical factor for electric vehicles — had not been adequately investigated before this study, despite years of intense ASSB research focused on ionic conductivity, interfaces and cycle life.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A blind spot in the field's benchmarking set: due diligence on ASSB developers should demand open-circuit voltage-decay and calendar-loss data, not just cycling curves.
insights.quote: However, their self-discharge behaviour, a critical factor for EVs, has not been adequately investigated so far.

insights.claim: The self-discharge conclusion is supported by both numerical simulation of self-discharge as a function of solid electrolyte electronic conductivity and thickness and by experimental verification on all-solid-state cells, rather than by modelling alone.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Simulation plus experimental confirmation raises the odds the 10^-12 S cm^-1 threshold becomes an accepted design specification rather than a contested claim.
insights.quote: Fig. 2: Simulation of the physical self-discharge behaviour of ASSBs as a function of the electronic conductivity and thickness of inorganic SSEs.Fig. 3: Experimental verification of self-discharge of ASSBs.

insights.claim: Suppressing physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries requires reducing the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte to approximately 10^-12 S cm^-1 — three to four orders of magnitude below what typical inorganic solid electrolytes deliver today.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A hard, testable materials specification: screen any ASSB electrolyte claim against 10^-12 S cm^-1 electronic conductivity, not just against ionic conductivity headlines.
insights.quote: To mitigate this physical self-discharge, the electronic conductivity of SSEs needs to be reduced to approximately 10−12 S cm−1.

insights.claim: None of the prevalent inorganic solid-state electrolyte families — the sulfides, halides, garnets, antiperovskites and complex hydrides surveyed in the study — meets the roughly 10^-12 S cm^-1 electronic conductivity threshold needed to avoid physical self-discharge.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Implies every current ASSB electrolyte chemistry carries an unresolved shelf-life liability, a reason to discount aggressive solid-state commercialization timelines for EV packs.
insights.quote: However, none of the prevalent SSEs meets this threshold.
insights.locator: Abstract, following the 10−12 S cm−1 threshold

insights.claim: The study benchmarks ionic against electronic conductivity across typical inorganic solid electrolytes side by side, making the electronic-conductivity axis — normally reported as an afterthought — a first-class selection criterion for solid electrolytes.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives investors a two-axis screen for solid electrolyte startups: high ionic conductivity alone is no longer a differentiator without a matching electronic-conductivity number.
insights.quote: Fig. 1: Comparative analysis of ionic and electronic conductivities of typical inorganic SSEs.

insights.claim: High electronic conductivity within solid electrolytes has separately been identified as the origin of lithium dendrite formation, meaning the same material property drives both self-discharge and the dendrite failure mode that limits solid-state lithium-metal cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: One lever fixes two failure modes — makes low-electronic-conductivity electrolyte IP disproportionately valuable relative to single-problem fixes.
insights.quote: High electronic conductivity as the origin of lithium dendrite formation within solid electrolytes.
insights.locator: References, Han, F. et al., Nat. Energy 4, 187–196 (2019)

insights.claim: Reducing physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries will require not only new solid electrolytes with lower electronic conductivity but also rational interface and full-cell designs, per the authors' stated conclusion.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A multi-front fix lengthens the ASSB development path; single-material breakthroughs are unlikely to be sufficient for EV-grade shelf life.
insights.quote: reducing physical self-discharge in ASSBs will require the development of SSEs with lower electronic conductivity, alongside rational interface and full-cell designs in future research

insights.claim: The authors present multiscale strategies to mitigate physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries, indicating mitigation is framed as spanning material, interface and cell length scales rather than a single formulation change.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Suggests value capture in ASSB is distributed across electrolyte, coating and cell-architecture suppliers rather than concentrated in the electrolyte material alone.
insights.quote: Fig. 4: Multiscale strategies to mitigate physical self-discharge in ASSBs.

insights.claim: The authors assert their self-discharge findings may reshape the future design and development of all-solid-state batteries, positioning self-discharge alongside ionic conductivity and interfacial stability as a core ASSB design constraint.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Watch for self-discharge and calendar-loss metrics entering ASSB benchmarking standards and OEM qualification specs over the next cycles.
insights.quote: This study provides critical insights into the self-discharge phenomenon of ASSBs, which may reshape their future design and development.

insights.claim: The all-solid-state battery self-discharge study is authored by a China-Canada group spanning the Eastern Institute of Technology's Zhejiang Key Laboratory of All-Solid-State Battery in Ningbo, the University of Western Ontario (Xueliang Sun), Xi'an Jiaotong University and Zhejiang University, with industrial participation from GLABAT Solid-State Battery Inc. and Carl Zeiss (Shanghai).
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Industrial co-authorship from a solid-state battery company and a metrology vendor signals the self-discharge problem is already reaching commercial development and characterization workflows.

insights.so_what: Maps where the ASSB knowledge base is being built with public money — relevant to who sets the technical standards and captures the resulting IP.

insights.claim: The manuscript was received on 6 February 2023 and accepted only on 20 May 2026, an unusually long review cycle for a Nature Energy paper that suggests the self-discharge claim was heavily contested or extensively revised before publication.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Signals the finding faced real resistance from the field; expect rebuttals and replication attempts rather than immediate consensus adoption.
